_doc: scripts/check-external-origin-csp.mjs — declared exemptions for the REVERSE direction.
The forward direction (an element references an origin the CSP forbids) has no exemptions
and never will: that is the class the gate exists for, and it fails SILENTLY in a browser.
The reverse direction (a CSP origin that nothing in landing/**/*.html references) is the
'we widened the policy for something we later removed' class. It has legitimate exceptions —
an origin whose consumer is not an element or a literal in our own HTML — and each one is
listed here WITH A REASON. An exemption without a stated reason gets deleted by the next
wave enforcing the contract, so the reason is the point.
_directives_doc: Scanned directives are exactly those whose consumers are elements or literals in our own
landing HTML: script-src, frame-src, style-src, connect-src.
font-src is deliberately NOT scanned. Its only origin, https://fonts.gstatic.com, is
requested by the Google Fonts STYLESHEET, not by anything in our markup — so scanning it
would produce a permanent false DRIFT on a healthy policy, and a gate that cries wolf once
is ignored forever. img-src is not scanned for the same reason plus its `https:` wildcard.
default-src / base-uri / form-action / object-src / frame-ancestors carry no external
origins today; if one ever does, add it here deliberately rather than by widening a glob.

reverse_exemptions.reason: SELFHOST-PLAUSIBLE-CE-AND-CF-ORIGIN-SHIELD: analytics is a FIRST-PARTY beacon — landing pages load /js/insights.js and POST /pa/event through the apex Caddy proxy, so the plausible origin appears in ZERO landing HTML files by design (measured 2026-08-27: 0 of 57). The connect-src allowance predates the proxy flip and is now unreferenced from our markup. NOT this wave's to remove: deciding whether the direct-origin path is still needed belongs to whoever owns the beacon. Recorded so it is a DECLARED gap rather than one rediscovered by the next incident.
